New PILL_PHASE_HEIGHT table (lean:14/normal:18/tall:26) resolved via the existing resolvePhaseSize ladder (t19), now newly read for in-lane pills too (previously only the PROGRAM-band phase bar read it) — composes as a per-sub-row floor, never multiplied down by a lean lane's density factor, so a tall pill still reads tall in a lean lane. Retired use-auto-lane-height.ts entirely (shrink-based, divided viewport evenly across a flat lane count that no longer makes sense once lanes can have their own different Lane Row heights) for new use-fit-to-screen.ts (expand-only; new localStorage key `wayframe:fit-to-screen`, old key abandoned as an accepted viewer-preference churn) — renamed end-to-end through RoadmapTimeline's `fitToScreen` prop, RoadmapWorkspace's toggle/wiring, and use-saved-views.ts's `fitToScreenEnabled` snapshot field (old `autoLaneHeightEnabled` field name retired, same churn-acceptable reasoning). pillSubRowOffset rewritten to center the whole stack of Lane-Row sub-row bands (previously always exactly one band) on the lane's own midpoint, verified by hand that a document with zero explicit laneRow assignments produces byte-identical output to today (bucketRows then yields exactly one row). Added 5 RoadmapTimeline-level regression tests (mixed point-marker+pill lanes, override-not-seed row reassignment, same-row collision safety, fitToScreen renders without throwing) plus 13 new lane-rows.ts unit tests covering every one of the prototype's own guided-walkthrough scenarios. tsc/eslint/vitest (469 tests, +18 new) all clean; no live browser click-through this session (claude-in-chrome can't reach this sandbox's localhost, per earlier tickets' same caveat) — worth a manual visual check of a real multi-pill lane before relying on this further, particularly the new default lane-height shrink for pills-only lanes.

t16.note: Membership, permissions & unauthenticated access — three roles (owner/editor/viewer) held per-identity on a Portfolio, enforced server-side at the Partykit room, never trusted from the client. New tables (src/lib/db/schema.ts, mirrored in party/src/db.ts): portfolios, portfolio_members (portfolio_id+identity -> role), portfolio_share_links (token -> portfolio_id+role, editor/viewer only — a public link is a mechanism, not a fourth role). src/lib/db/portfolios.ts exposes createPortfolioWithOwner/setMember/removeMember/getRole/getRoleForProgram/createShareLink/resolveShareLink (7 tests). src/lib/auth/room-token.ts mints/verifies a short-lived HMAC-SHA256 identity token (Web Crypto, not a JWT lib, so the same verify logic runs unmodified in party/'s Cloudflare Worker runtime too — party/src/room-token.ts duplicates the verify half, same package-boundary tradeoff as db.ts; the auth.ts secret export is duplicated as a literal rather than imported since pulling in next-auth's bootstrap broke vitest's module resolution) — the token proves identity only, never a role, so party/src/membership.ts's resolveProgramRole/resolveShareLinkRole always looks up the current role fresh from the DB rather than trusting anything the token or client asserts. party/src/index.ts wires an onBeforeConnect (runs in the Worker, before the Durable Object) that verifies `?token=` or resolves `?shareToken=`, rejects with 403 before the WebSocket upgrade on any failure (this is also how an uninvited unsigned-in visitor never gets a hosted room — 'never a hosted row' per the gist), and forwards the resolved role via a request header the DO's onConnect reads into per-connection state; ProgramRoom.isReadOnly (y-partyserver's real write-gating hook, wired into its own sync-protocol handling) returns true for viewer connections, blocking writes while still allowing sync reads and awareness/presence. Also fixed a real latent bug while touching onConnect: it previously fully overrode YServer's onConnect (the sync-step1 + awareness handshake every new connection needs) without calling super, meaning a second client joining an already-running room never received the room's existing state — now calls super.onConnect after capturing the role. New GET /api/rooms/[programId]/token route mints an identity token for a signed-in caller with a resolvable role (401 unsigned-in, 403 no role); a share-link guest never calls this route, connecting straight with its shareToken instead. src/lib/realtime/provider.ts's connectProgramRoom gains a RoomAccess param ({token: () => Promise<string>} refreshed on every reconnect, matching a short TTL, or {shareToken} for guests) — still otherwise unconsumed, same scaffolded-until-the-client<->Yjs-bridge-exists caveat t4/t13/t36 carry. `wayframe:edit-lock` needed no code change: its access-control half is superseded by the above, its presentation-preference half is already an ordinary viewer preference and stays as-is — documented as a new CONTEXT.md doctrine section (#90) plus Role/Guest Session glossary entries, since CONTEXT.md had zero membership/permissions vocabulary before this. tsc (main app + party's own tsconfig)/eslint/vitest (388 tests, +12 new) all clean; no live wrangler dev two-client re-verification of isReadOnly done this session — worth a manual check before this gets wired into real UI.

t17.note: Migration of today's artifacts — only `wayframe:document` actually needed migrating (already a PortfolioDocument per t11, not a bare RoadmapData). Added the previously-missing storage for it: portfolios.content (new DB column, src/lib/db/schema.ts) holds the Portfolio-level shared fields as JSON (setPortfolioContent/getPortfolioContent), and program-storage.ts's new createProgramFromData seeds a brand-new `programs` row as a whole-Program-blob bulk seed inside a fresh Y.Doc (single `program` Y.Map key) — the real field-level Program-JSON-to-Y.Map bridge still doesn't exist anywhere (confirmed against party/src/index.ts's own comment on this), so this is an honest interim encoding, matching the same 'legitimate bulk seed' reasoning t35's own gist already uses for AI-extraction's new-Program case. New idempotent POST /api/portfolios/migrate-local (src/app/api/portfolios/migrate-local/route.ts): signed-in only, validates the posted PortfolioDocument via the same validatePortfolioDocument file-open already uses, no-ops to the existing Portfolio if getOwnedPortfolioId(identity) already resolves one (the real correctness guarantee — a second browser signing in with the same identity must land on the same Portfolio, not create a duplicate), otherwise creates one via createPortfolioWithOwner (t16's primitive, finally wired to a route) and seeds every Program from the posted document. Client half: src/lib/auth/use-migrate-local-portfolio.ts fires once an authenticated session is observed, reading the local document and POSTing it — a `wayframe:portfolio-migrated` localStorage flag is a per-browser optimization only, not the correctness guarantee. Real scope finding: the app had zero sign-in UI anywhere (t5 only built the NextAuth server plumbing), so there was no way to ever reach an authenticated client state to trigger this — asked the user how to handle that gap; they chose adding real minimal plumbing over leaving it unwired. Added SessionProviderWrapper (client-boundary wrapper since layout.tsx is a server component exporting metadata) and AuthControls (fixed-position sign in/out control, deliberately undesigned — explicitly flagged as plumbing a future ticket may replace), wired into layout.tsx/page.tsx. Also resolved the '.wayframe.json vs .wayframeportfolio.json' design question document-file.ts's own header comment had been flagging as still-open since t11: `.wayframe.json` keeps its existing PortfolioDocument schema unchanged (no redesign) as the Program-level interchange format; new sibling src/lib/document-file/portfolio-export.ts adds the `.wayframeportfolio.json` whole-Portfolio container (same PortfolioDocument shape, no new type needed — programs is already an N-length array) — deliberately unconsumed, no export UI yet, same treatment t4/t13/t36 got. The 26 wayframe:* viewer-preference keys needed no code at all per the gist (already per-browser/unscoped/content-free). Implemented by a fork given a fully-specified file-by-file spec (t14's pattern); verified independently afterward rather than trusting its report — reviewed every diff and re-ran tsc/eslint/vitest myself. tsc/eslint/vitest (401 tests, +13 new) all clean.

t19.note: Style resolution order & locked property set — full build, not just the data model: every one of the 8 locked properties (marker shape, marker scale, per-item font scale, title/date label position, show/hide, per-item color, phase shape, phase size) now resolves through a real precedence ladder AND renders through it, not just scaffolded. Before this ticket only per-item color had any resolution logic at all (a 2-rung function, milestones-only, TopLevelItems got none of it); the other 7 properties had zero rendering support anywhere (markers were always diamonds, phases were always pills). New src/components/timeline/style-resolution.ts holds the ladder as pure functions (resolveMarkerShape/resolveMarkerScale/resolveFontScale/resolveTitleLabelPosition/resolveDateLabelPosition/resolveHidden/resolvePhaseShape/resolvePhaseSize/resolveMarkerColor, 31 tests) — most-specific-wins per the gist: item styleOverride > identity-scoped color (color only) > Program.styleDefaults (new field) > Theme token (Theme gained markerShapeDefault/markerScaleDefault/phaseShapeDefault/phaseSizeDefault, all set to today's hardcoded values so a document with no override anywhere renders byte-identical to before this ticket — proven by all 432 pre-existing tests passing unmodified). resolveMarkerColor replaces the old 2-rung resolveMarkerPaint with the full 4-rung ladder, byte-identical regression-tested against the old function's output. Types.ts/schema.ts gained StyleOverride (.strict() Zod + compile-time Equals<> assertion) on Milestone, TopLevelItem's milestone/phase variants (not annotation), and Program.styleDefaults; also caught and fixed a real cross-file drift in src/lib/scenario/types.ts's TopLevelItemPatch, which needed the same field to stay in sync with the schema. RoadmapTimeline.tsx: CushionMarker generalized from one hardcoded rotated-rect to a shape-dispatching renderer (star/flag/square/rectangle/circle/diamond, all parameterized purely by (cx,cy,r) so the existing bigger-r-for-a-ring pattern works unmodified for any shape), threaded through all 5 marker-ring call sites plus the main fill; MilestoneMarker gained a program prop, per-item font-scale composed multiplicatively on top of the global viewer font-scale (not substituting for it, per the gist) across every one of a milestone's own text elements including its GhostBadge; titleLabelPosition/dateLabelPosition bypass the tiered collision-avoidance layout entirely when set, rendering one fixed-offset label in the chosen compass direction instead (deliberately NOT collision-aware against other labels — an editorial escape hatch, not a reimplementation of the layout engine); hidden suppresses a milestone/TopLevelItem's own marker + its own at-risk projection only, not connectors/critical-path/ghost-badge layout math (a lighter-weight toggle than t22's future lane-hide, deliberately). Phase shape (pill vs 3px-corner rectangle) and phase size (lean 0.75x / normal / tall 1.35x, the lean ratio mirroring Swimlane.density's existing precedent) wired into the PROGRAM-band phase pill's height/corner-radius. Scope boundaries, all deliberate: no editing UI for any of this (t34, downstream in the dependency graph, owns that — this ticket only makes existing/test-constructed styleOverride values resolve and render correctly); no color ladder for TopLevelItems (no categoryId/identity-color concept exists for them); phase color stays theme.statusColor-only, untouched. Implemented as two sequential forks (data model+ladder, then rendering wiring) given the ticket's size — each independently verified against its own diff and re-run tsc/eslint/vitest before trusting it, continuing this session's standing practice. tsc/eslint/vitest (437 tests, +36 total across both forks) all clean.

t35.note: AI pipeline: extract into an existing Portfolio's new Program — landed ahead of its original queue position, pulled forward after a survey of sibling ticket t39 (deterministic CSV/XLSX/Smartsheet import retargeting) found t39's own gist leans on this ticket's 'allocate-id-and-write-one-Program-row' primitive without listing t35 as a formal blocker — same kind of gap flagged for t16/t17's ordering earlier this session; asked the user, who chose to land t35 first. Per the gist: extraction itself (/api/extract) stays fully portfolio-unaware, unchanged — everything changes in apply. New POST /api/portfolios/[portfolioId]/programs/extract (auth-gated via getRole, owner/editor only) takes /api/extract's existing response body, allocates a Program id (nanoid) and a non-atomic 'next order' (listProgramSnapshotsForPortfolio(...).length — same single-writer heuristic t12's own primitives already assume elsewhere), and writes it as a legitimate bulk seed via createProgramFromData (the primitive t17's migrate-local route already established, now with its second real caller). The one place apply genuinely touches shared Portfolio state — legendCategories — got a new src/lib/db/portfolios.ts primitive, appendLegendCategories: merges by name (never a wholesale overwrite, so it can't stomp a category another Program already references) and returns an id-remap Map the route uses to rewrite any of the new Program's milestone.categoryId fields that pointed at a since-deduped draft category — a referential-integrity detail the gist's prose didn't spell out mechanically but which 'additive, never stomping' requires once actually implemented. Correction ops needed no code change at all: verified /api/correct is fully stateless (client-supplied refs in, a patch out, no DB touch), so 'Portfolio-scoped correction ops' is exactly the gist's own 'category error' — landed as a doctrine comment on PatchOpSchema instead of a schema change. Full build, not just backend (the user's explicit scope choice, mirroring t18/t19's precedent over t13/t36's scaffold-unconsumed treatment): new GET /api/portfolios/mine + client hook use-owned-portfolio-id.ts (both null-safe for 'not signed in' and 'signed in but owns no Portfolio yet', the latter a real pre-existing gap since t17's migrate-local only creates a Portfolio when local content exists to migrate) let ImportPanel's existing AI-extraction tab offer a real 'Add as a new Program in my Portfolio' checkbox, branching extract() to the new route and showing an inline confirmation instead of ImportPanel's existing replace-and-close behavior when checked (that existing behavior is completely untouched when the checkbox is off or the toggle isn't shown). Implemented by a fork given a fully-specified, file-by-file spec (t14/t17/t19's pattern) after an upfront research pass mapped every real touchpoint (extraction's two existing entry flows, createProgramFromData's exact signature, portfolios.ts's content-merge posture, the getRole auth pattern from rooms/[programId]/token) rather than guessing signatures; verified independently afterward per the standing 'never trust a fork's report alone' practice — read every diff against the spec and re-ran tsc/eslint/vitest myself. tsc/eslint clean; vitest 441/441 (+4 new, all in portfolios.test.ts covering appendLegendCategories: new-content seed, name-based dedup-and-remap, a mixed new+existing call, and the empty-array no-op). t39 (deterministic import retargeting) is next up, now genuinely unblocked.

t39.note: Deterministic import retargeting (CSV/XLSX/Smartsheet) — the gist's premise-check confirmed the CSV/XLSX path already did the right thing (SpreadsheetImportTab/rowsToRoadmap diffs rows against the live document and commits {newLanes, adds, updateOps} atomically via importMerge, no whole-document replace); Smartsheet was the actual bug, routed through ImportPanel's 'AI extraction' combined-text tab into /api/extract despite fetchSheetRows already returning the identical ParsedRow[] shape rowsToRoadmap consumes. Fixed by folding Smartsheet into SpreadsheetImportTab as a second row source (its connect/select/pull state and UI moved there wholesale) and retiring its AI-extraction routing entirely — ImportPanel now has just two tabs (AI extraction from free text; deterministic Spreadsheet covering CSV/XLSX/Smartsheet), with the old three-tab 'smartsheet' tab and its sheetSource/includeSheet state deleted. Portfolio-targeting added to SpreadsheetImportTab per the gist's asymmetry: rowsToRoadmap is natively an 'existing Program update' tool (title+lane matching only means something against a live document), so the 'new Program' case matches rows against a module-level EMPTY_SEED_PROGRAM constant instead of the live `data` prop — every row falls through to `adds`, nothing to update against — then commits by POSTing a RoadmapDocument-shaped payload (programName/generatedAt/owner/bluf/actionItems/swimlanes/topLevelItems/milestones, no id/portfolioId/order/schemaVersion/legendCategories — all either unused or overwritten server-side) to t35's existing POST /api/portfolios/[portfolioId]/programs/extract route, reusing its allocate-id-and-write-one-Program-row primitive directly rather than duplicating it. No legendCategories concern on this path (rowsToRoadmap never produces categoryId), confirming the gist's 'swimlanes are Program-local, no additive Portfolio-state write needed' claim — appendLegendCategories is never called. New UI: a checkbox ('Add as a new Program in my Portfolio') gated on useOwnedPortfolioId, a new-Program-name text input, and an applying/error/created-confirmation flow mirroring ImportPanel's own AI-extraction toggle (t35's precedent), reusing DiffBanner for the accept/reject review either way. Existing-Program update path (onMerge/importMerge) is completely unchanged. Added one regression test to rows-to-roadmap.test.ts documenting the empty-seed behavior explicitly (every row becomes an add, zero updates, __newLaneName always set). No fork delegated — small enough (2 component files + 1 test) to implement directly after reading every touchpoint (rowsToRoadmap, fetchSheetRows' ParsedRow shape, the t35 route's exact destructuring, useOwnedPortfolioId) myself. tsc/eslint/vitest (442 tests, +1 new) all clean.

t40.note: Binary asset storage boundary — the gist keeps today's no-blob-store posture rather than replacing it: companyLogo.dataUrl / attachments[].url stay inline strings inside the Program's Yjs document, riding along in t12's per-Program snapshot row with zero asset-specific code, since object storage with a reference would make (capital-S) Snapshot immutability expensive (either the referenced object can never be GC'd, or every Snapshot needs its own copy-on-write). A research pass confirmed the only file-upload path that actually writes a dataUrl into persisted document content is RoadmapWorkspace's company-logo upload (handleUploadLogo) — Milestone/TopLevelItem attachments are added via AttachmentEditor as a plain typed URL (a link, or a manually-pasted data URL), no file-picker of their own, so no upload surface exists there to guard. EntryForm's whiteboard-photo upload is a separate, out-of-scope data flow: it feeds /api/extract transiently and never becomes companyLogo/attachments content. The one concrete deliverable the gist calls for — 'a sane client-side max-upload-size guardrail, same posture as any other size validation' — landed as MAX_LOGO_BYTES (2MB) in RoadmapWorkspace.tsx: handleUploadLogo now rejects an oversized file via the existing fileError toast (reused as-is, no new UI) before it ever reaches FileReader/setCompanyLogo. Implemented directly, no fork — a single-handler, single-file change once the research pass ruled out a second upload surface. Two new tests (RoadmapWorkspace.test.tsx): oversized upload leaves companyLogo unset (button stays 'Upload') and shows the inline error; an under-cap upload succeeds (button flips to 'Replace'), no false-positive rejection. tsc/eslint/vitest (444 tests, +2 new) all clean.
